subject: Regional tariff misclassification & ingest attribution — request for credit and VAT invoice
messages:
From: Kai Morales <kai@bytewave.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bytewave.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden EU tariff on Nov 28 - looking for explanation/credit

Hi Sofia,

We spotted a large unexpected charge on our Nov 28 invoice that appears billed at the EU regional tariff even though our traffic is routed from US regions. This pushed our month-end overage by ~22%.

Quick details:
- Account: ByteWave (BW-ENT-4301)
- Invoice period: Nov 1–30, 2026
- Spike window: Nov 28 02:30–03:15 UTC
- Observed impact: ~3.6M extra tokens attributed to EU tariff tier

Can you help confirm whether this is a metering attribution issue (requests routed through an EU edge) or a pricing misclassification? Procurement is asking for a breakdown and evidence to approve a partial credit. If you need an export, I can attach logs.

Thanks —
Kai Morales
Head of Platform
ByteWave
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Kai Morales <kai@bytewave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden EU tariff on Nov 28 - looking for explanation/credit

Thanks Kai — sorry for the surprise. I’ve looped in Ben (billing/instrumentation) and Soojin (account ops). We’ll pull a sampling export and a region-routing trace for the spike window.

Action items:
- Ben: can you validate whether the tokens were billed under EU tariff due to region-tagging or because the requests were actually processed in EU?
- Soojin: please prepare a provisional credit proposal we can offer while we investigate (byte-level evidence attached if available).

Kai — it would help if you can attach a couple of example request IDs or a short sample of client timestamps to cross-check. We’ll aim to have a preliminary answer within 24 hours.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kai Morales <kai@bytewave.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden EU tariff on Nov 28 - looking for explanation/credit

Hi all — I pulled the serving and routing traces for the Nov 28 02:00–04:00 UTC window. Key findings:

Summary (short):
- A small subset of ByteWave requests (approx 3.5M tokens) were routed through our EU fallback pool between 02:29:18–02:46:40 UTC after a transient edge outage in us-west-2.
- The requests were processed in EU hosts — meter records reflect EU region pricing.
- The traffic pattern shows repeated short-lived retries from one client IP that pushed token density during the failover window (likely a client-side retry policy + no prefix cache hit).

Evidence attached: redwood-hourly-export-20261128.csv (hourly attribution), bytewave_usage_samples.csv (5 request samples with request_id and timestamps).

Recommended remediation:
1) Offer a one-time microburst credit equal to the delta between EU tariff and US tariff for the impacted tokens. I’ve sketched a proposed credit in proposed-credit-summary.pdf (approx 22% of the spike).
2) For invoice correctness we can issue a credit memo against Nov invoice and generate an amended VAT breakdown if you need EU->US reclassification for tax purposes.
3) If ByteWave prefers, we can exclude the flagged request IDs from billed totals and reprocess the invoice.

Questions for ByteWave:
- Do you want a credit memo applied now (fast) or an amended invoice + VAT reissue (longer, needs tax team)?
- Can you confirm whether the client retry behavior is something you want us to exclude in future attribution rules? We can add a conservative dedupe window for retries to avoid similar microbursts being billed at fallback tariffs.

Ben Carter
Principal Billing Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-hourly-export-20261128.csv, bytewave_usage_samples.csv, proposed-credit-summary.pdf)
From: Kai Morales <kai@bytewave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bytewave.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden EU tariff on Nov 28 - looking for explanation/credit

Thanks Ben — the export and samples match what we see. Procurement prefers a credit memo applied now (fast path) for the difference and then a corrected VAT breakdown. They want the amended VAT invoice so internal AP can close the period.

We agree on the proposed microburst credit amount in the pdf. A few asks:
- Please confirm the credit memo reference once applied (we need it on our PO).
- For VAT reissue: ByteWave is registered in the US (no EU VAT liability), so if you issue an amended invoice showing the affected lines as US-sourced and remove EU VAT, we can process internally.
- We’ll follow up on the client retry behavior separately with our infra team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Kai Morales
Head of Platform, ByteWave
(kai@bytewave.ai)
